$comment: task-kit depends on plugins-kit:skills-kit for skills_kit_lib (schema_engine and document_walker, hard-imported by the task_system package) and on plugins-kit:awesome-kit because the task CLI's work verb emits Skill(awesome-kit:orchestrate) as the always-required baseline skill; skills-kit and awesome-kit are auto-installed when missing. bootstrap_lib has no direct import here: the vendored bootstrap_guard is stdlib-only. llm_kit comes from the katsoft-llm-kit package that pyproject.toml pins (extras config, sdk, local), not from a shared-lib link; the answer engine imports it lazily (llm_kit.dispatch.declaration.run) to answer questions, including the orientation question the review verb asks. llm-kit has no plugin install edge: if llm_kit is not importable the answer engine reports an actionable provisioning diagnostic instead of answering, and every other verb works. requires_bootstrap is 0.160.0, the bootstrap that revokes the undeclared llm_kit link and stamps the released-package venv, so a venv never holds both the link and the package. psutil stays in the venv for the cross-platform process identity that procstamp.py and harness.py read, and openai stays in check_imports for the transport answerers the package's sdk extra installs. bin/ is synced to the data directory and that directory is put on PATH (path_entries), so task-kit works in any terminal; the synced copy is a thin locator that runs the newest installed version from the plugin cache, and it uses the marketplace name plugins-kit exactly as the plugin's other data paths do.
